Methods for nbreg fits

Source: R/methods.R
nbreg-methods.Rd

Standard S3 methods for objects returned by nbreg().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.nbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
residuals(object, type = c("response", "pearson"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
predict(object, newdata = NULL, type = c("response", "link"), ...)

Arguments

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

...

Not used.

object, x

An "nbreg" object (or its summary for print).

type

For residuals(): "response" (\(y - \hat\mu\)) or "pearson" (\((y - \hat\mu)/\sqrt{\hat\mu + \hat\mu^2/\hat\theta}\)). For predict(): "response" (\(\hat\mu\)) or "link" (\(\hat\eta = \log\hat\mu\)).

newdata

Optional data frame to predict for. Offsets are evaluated in newdata.

Value

coef() a named vector; vcov() a matrix; logLik() a "logLik" object with df = number of coefficients + 1 (for \(\theta\)), so AIC() and BIC() work; fitted(), residuals() and predict() numeric vectors; nobs() the number of observations; summary() an object of class "summary.nbreg".

Examples

set.seed(2)
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(200))
d$y <- rnbinom(200, size = 1.5, mu = exp(0.5 + 0.8 * d$x))
fit <- nbreg(y ~ x, data = d)
fit
#> 
#> Call:
#> nbreg(formula = y ~ x, data = d)
#> 
#> Negative binomial (NB2) regression, IRLS + Newton-Raphson for theta
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#> (Intercept)            x  
#>      0.4832       0.8673  
#> 
#> Theta: 1.414 (SE 0.2772)
#> Log-likelihood: -360.955 on 3 Df
#> 
coef(fit)
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>   0.4832092   0.8673129 
sqrt(diag(vcov(fit)))
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>  0.08843103  0.08225032 
AIC(fit); BIC(fit)
#> [1] 727.9105
#> [1] 737.8054
head(residuals(fit, type = "pearson"))
#>           1           2           3           4           5           6 
#> -0.69848201  0.04582069  0.43126187 -0.65218147  0.27572733 -0.89198443 
predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(x = c(-1, 0, 1)))
#>         1         2         3 
#> 0.6810608 1.6212690 3.8594399
